concepts.name: ThreadPoolExecutor
concepts.description: ThreadPoolExecutor runs callables in worker threads and is a natural fit for overlapping blocking I/O; CPU-bound behavior depends on whether CPython is GIL-enabled or free-threaded.

concepts.name: ProcessPoolExecutor
concepts.description: ProcessPoolExecutor uses separate worker processes to side-step one process's GIL for suitable CPU-bound work, while requiring process-boundary values and callables to be serializable/importable.

concepts.name: concurrent.futures.as_completed
concepts.description: `as_completed()` yields Future objects as they finish, allowing completion-order handling; `Future.result()` returns the value or re-raises the worker exception.

concepts.name: threading.Event
concepts.description: `threading.Event` is a thread-safe signal flag: `wait()` blocks until set, `set()` wakes waiters and leaves the flag true, and `clear()` resets it.

concepts.name: threading.Lock
concepts.description: `threading.Lock` provides mutual exclusion around thread-shared critical sections and should protect application invariants instead of relying on the GIL.

concepts.name: queue.Queue for threads
concepts.description: `queue.Queue` is a synchronized producer-consumer queue for threads; bounded queues provide backpressure and `task_done()`/`join()` track unfinished work.

concepts.name: Explicit multiprocessing start context
concepts.description: `multiprocessing.get_context()` explicitly selects process start semantics; defaults vary by platform/version, including Python 3.14's POSIX switch from fork to forkserver.
